citations.quote: ECOG 3, labs acceptable for systemic therapy

candidates.description: A standardized scale used to assess the functional status of a patient, where higher scores indicate greater disability.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Extract the numeric ECOG performance status value as reported in the assessment or history section of the clinical note.
candidates.measurement_definition: The reported ECOG score (0-4) documented in the oncology assessment or history of present illness.
candidates.name: ECOG Performance Status
candidates.uncertainty: The assessment is clinician-reported and may vary in subjectivity between providers.

candidates.description: A ratio calculated by dividing the absolute neutrophil count by the absolute lymphocyte count, often used as a proxy for systemic inflammation.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Identify the 'NLR' or 'Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio' value in the laboratory results section.
candidates.measurement_definition: The numeric value of the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) derived from the most recent baseline CBC.
candidates.name: Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio (NLR)
candidates.uncertainty: Varying timepoints for lab draws across different chunks for the same patient may make the definition of 'baseline' inconsistent.

limitations: Small sample of patients provided in the retrieval evidence.
NLR is not reported for all patients, limiting its availability as a baseline variable.
ECOG status is a subjective clinical assessment.
summary: The evidence identifies functional performance status (ECOG PS) and the Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio (NLR) as measurable baseline clinical variables associated with patients with non-small cell lung cancer prior to systemic therapy.
